packageRules.description: The AWS SDK ships ~35 separately versioned modules that release in lockstep. Ungrouped, they would never drain at prConcurrentLimit 1.

The workflows' go-version inputs (depName `go`) and the two .tool-versions pins (depNames `golang` and `golangci-lint`) all track the same toolchain; bump them in one PR. golangci-lint especially cannot lag: it type-checks through a vendored x/tools that only reads export data from Go releases it already knows about.

A pin fixes a floating tag to the version already in use, so there is no newer release to age. Renovate synthesizes pin updates with no releaseTimestamp, and the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour of timestamp-required holds those pending forever.

Go indirect dependencies are disabled by default, which also silently swallows their security advisories: x/crypto sat on 33 CVEs with skipReason `disabled` and no update. Enable them so advisories can reach them, but park the routine ones behind a dashboard checkbox — there are ~40 and none earns a PR on its own. The vulnerabilityAlerts config force-sets dependencyDashboardApproval to false, so an indirect dep with a CVE still gets an immediate PR, and skips both minimumReleaseAge and the concurrency limits.

The aws sdk group above drains 14 direct modules in one PR. Enabling indirect updates would pull in 15 indirect siblings carrying dependencyDashboardApproval, mixing approval-gated upgrades into that branch; leave them disabled so the group keeps flowing as it does today.
